evals.prompt: set up a trivy scan gate in our pipeline
evals.expected_output: Scans at build time before push rather than only at rest, defines a severity-and-fix-availability gate policy (block critical/high with a fix, warn without one, log medium/low) instead of blocking on raw CVE count, and enables secret scanning alongside CVE scanning as an automatic block.

evals.prompt: we have 300 open findings and nobody's triaging them
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses noise from an unfiltered severity gate and recommends sorting by upgrade-available first, filtering by reachability where the scanner supports it, and replacing silent ignores with documented, time-boxed exceptions that have an owner and review date.

evals.prompt: let's block the build on every single CVE, no exceptions
evals.expected_output: Pushes back that blocking on every CVE regardless of exploitability or fix availability trains engineers to route around the scanner, and recommends gating by severity plus whether a fix exists and the code path is reachable, per a written policy rather than an ad hoc threshold.
